finalText:
Migration finished.

## What changed

12 files were still on `db.query`, spread across five packages:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `repo/session.js`, `service/teamService.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |

36 call sites in total (three per file: get-by-id, list, update), rewritten from `db.query(sql, params)` to `db.execute({ sql, params })`. The result is byte-identical in shape to the already-migrated siblings — e.g. `support/src/repo/sla.js` now matches `support/src/repo/macro.js` line for line.

## Two things I deliberately did not touch

**`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js`** still has 2 `db.query` calls (lines 9 and 13). The file header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, "Do not edit — it is replaced wholesale on every upgrade, and local changes are silently lost." Editing it would be undone by the next upgrade, so this needs to be handled elsewhere: upstream fix, a shim, or dropping the dependency. Worth flagging because `lib/db.js` says the driver's next major removes `query` entirely — so this is a real break, just not one a sweep can fix. Let me know if you want me to look at how widely the adapter is actually used.

**`cache.query(...)`** — 25 call sites, one in each `repo/*.js`. Despite the name, this is a method on the `cache` object from `lib/cache.js`, unrelated to the db driver. All 25 are still present and unmodified.

## Verification

- `db.query` no longer appears anywhere outside `vendor/`.
- `node --check` passes on all 78 JS files; all files still end in a trailing newline.
- Runtime check: required all 75 package modules and invoked every exported `get*ById` / `list*` / `update*` / `cached*` — 250 calls producing 325 driver calls, of which **0** used the legacy `query` form and 0 had a missing or malformed `sql`/`params`. That confirms the `params` arrays survived the rewrite intact, including the awkward `[...keys.map((k) => patch[k]), id]` spread in the update paths.

There's no test suite or build config in the repo, so the runtime check above is the strongest available signal.
